title: Calculate “The Number”: Finding Your Financial Freedom Point
opening: Estimate a resource target, then compare the assumptions that produce it. What would “enough” make possible in your life?

labels.annualNet: Annual spending to cover, before tax assumption
labels.annualGross: Annual amount after tax gross-up assumption
labels.invalidReturn: Enter a return above 0% to calculate a finite scenario. Zero or negative returns do not produce this target.
labels.invalidTaxMultiplier: Use a gross-up multiplier of 1 or more: 1 adds no amount; 2 doubles annual spending. It is not a tax rate.
labels.invalidInput: Enter a non-negative amount using digits and an optional decimal point.
labels.countInput: Enter a whole number of dependents (0 or more).
labels.assumptionNote: The multiplier is an explicit scenario input, not a tax rate. A multiplier of 2 doubles the annual spending estimate. The real return is after inflation; enter the return you want to compare.
labels.outcome: What would reaching this amount let you do?
labels.reflection: Reflect on what this estimate is for
labels.check: A spreadsheet gives a precise number. Does that establish a reliable future income? Explain what the calculation shows and what it leaves uncertain.
labels.private: This practice is private to you. Save it only if you want a copy.

source.excerpt: Estimate monthly expenses, add omitted costs and account for dependents. Multiply by twelve to obtain annual expenses. State a tax assumption separately. Divide by a chosen return after inflation to create an invested-assets scenario. Compare different expense, tax and return assumptions. Then examine what “enough” would make possible in your life.
source.boundary: This arithmetic is a scenario, not a promise, safe withdrawal rule, investment recommendation or financial plan. The inputs do not establish future returns, taxes, volatility, duration or financial adequacy.

example.title: Same spending, different return assumptions
example.body: At $2,000 monthly net spending, with no omitted costs, dependents or tax gross-up, annual spending is $24,000. Dividing by assumed real returns of 2%, 3% and 6% gives $1,200,000, $800,000 and $400,000. This is arithmetic from stated inputs; none of the figures is certified as enough or safe.
